analyzed_vuln.description: `get_coffset` retrieves the compressed offsets table from an untrusted frame but discards its actual available/compressed length by calling the legacy size-less `blosc_getitem`. That wrapper passes `INT32_MAX` as `srcsize` to `_blosc_getitem`, so malformed offsets-chunk metadata and block-start entries are treated as though they point into a huge valid buffer. The attacker-controlled block offset is propagated to `blosc_d`, which advances `src` outside the input and crashes when `sw32_` reads the per-stream compressed size at blosc2.c:1124. The root fix belongs in `get_coffset`: obtain and validate the offsets-table byte length (including against the frame boundary) and use a size-aware getitem/decompression path.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A crafted in-memory frame must pass `blosc2_frame_from_sframe` checks (declared frame length equals the supplied length and the trailer marker is valid) and have header values that produce at least one chunk processed by the harness. `header_len + cbytes` must leave enough bytes for `get_coffsets`' minimal extended-header check, but the offsets chunk can contain malicious size/block metadata—particularly an out-of-range `bstarts` entry. During chunk decompression, `frame_get_lazychunk` calls `get_coffset`; because the real remaining frame length is not supplied to `blosc_getitem`, its `INT32_MAX` pseudo-length allows the bad block offset through, leading to the invalid read in `blosc_d`.
